chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about breastfeeding (radāʿ), and he said: 'That which is prohibited due to it is prohibited just as lineage (nasab) is prohibited [from marriage].'

key_terms.اَلرَّضَاعِ: Breastfeeding; the act of nursing that creates kinship ties.
key_terms.اَلنَّسَبِ: Lineage; direct blood relationship, typically through birth.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect of breastfeeding on marriage prohibitions in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the legal effects of breastfeeding (radāʿ) mirror those of consanguinity (nasab), rendering the same relatives mahram. This ruling underscores the principle that milk kinship creates a permanent bond comparable to blood lineage, a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for determining marriage prohibitions. The statement reflects the broader Islamic legal theory that the physical act of nursing confers a status equivalent to natural descent in matters of inheritance and marriage.
